column1: # The shop's own vocabulary. Sits ABOVE Olam and wins over it.
# Olam is a general dictionary and it is wrong about this trade, confidently:
# it renders `flex` as മടക്കുക ("to fold"), `card` as തടിച്ച കടലാസ് ("thick
# paper"), and it has never heard of `standee`, `matte`, `visiting card` or
# `vinyl` at all. On a price list those are quotations for the wrong thing.
# Nearly every term here is an English loanword written in Malayalam script,
# because that is what Kerala print shops say out loud. Where a genuine
# Malayalam word is in ordinary use (ലഘുലേഖ for a pamphlet) it is used instead.
# REVIEW THIS FILE ONCE. It is short on purpose. Anything wrong can be fixed
# here, or overridden from the Word library panel in the Excel tab without
# Lines starting with # are ignored. Keep it sorted; keep it small.
# Olam has all of these, but as *definitions*: it renders `product` as
# ഫാക്ടറിയിൽ നിർമ്മിച്ച വസ്തു, "an item manufactured in a factory". True, and
# useless as a column header on a quotation.
# The headings of the sheets the shop is actually handed. They sit at the top of
# every column the client reads first, and Olam gets several of them plainly
# wrong: it renders `place` as സ്ഥാപിക്കുക, "to establish".
# Taken from `_UNIT_WORDS` in backend/features/translate.py, which is the form
# the review grid already checks a translation against. These two must agree:
# a unit the dictionary writes one way and the checker expects another way
